01-quantum-algorithmic-thinking: Every quantum algorithm begins with a precise specification of the computational problem, the input access model, the target output, and the allowed failure probability \(\varepsilon\).

Superposition alone does not solve problems; quantum advantage comes from steering amplitudes through unitary transformations so wrong branches cancel by destructive interference while target branches reinforce.
Honest resource accounting tracks oracle queries, two-qubit gate count, circuit depth, ancilla workspace, and classical pre- or post-processing separately.
02-coherent-computation: Any classical circuit can be made reversible using Toffoli gates and clean ancilla qubits so that \(|x,0,0\rangle \mapsto |x,w(x),f(x)\rangle\) preserves quantum coherence across superpositions.
Leftover workspace bits \(w(x)\) entangle with the input register and destroy interference unless they are uncomputed via Bennett’s compute–copy–uncompute trick.
Trading ancilla width against circuit depth changes the physical footprint of a subroutine without changing its logical action on the input and output registers.
03-phase-encoding: Applying a bit-flip oracle to a target prepared in \(|-\rangle = (|0\rangle - |1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}\) kicks the function value into the relative phase \((-1)^{f(x)}|x\rangle\) while leaving the ancilla unentangled.
Hadamard transforms convert global linear phase patterns \((-1)^{s\cdot x}\) into deterministic computational-basis outcomes, as in the Deutsch–Jozsa and Bernstein–Vazirani algorithms.
Continuous phase kickback \(e^{2\pi i g(x)/2^m}\) generalizes Boolean kickback to arithmetic functions and prepares the periodic states consumed by Fourier readout.
04-fourier-methods: The \(n\)-qubit Quantum Fourier Transform maps periodic superpositions with period \(r\) to sharp amplitude peaks near integer multiples of \(2^n/r\) using \(O(n^2)\) gates.

Quantum phase estimation combines controlled powers \(U^{2^k}\) with the inverse QFT to read out an eigenphase \(\varphi\) of \(U|\psi\rangle = e^{2\pi i\varphi}|\psi\rangle\) to \(m\) bits of precision.

Order finding and Shor’s factoring algorithm reduce integer factorization to estimating the eigenphases of modular multiplication \(|y\rangle \mapsto |ay \bmod N\rangle\) followed by continued-fraction post-processing.
05-amplitude-manipulation: Two reflections—one about the marked target subspace and one about the initial state \(A|0\rangle\)—compose into a planar rotation by angle \(2\theta\) in the two-dimensional span of good and bad states.

Amplitude amplification boosts an initial success probability \(p = \sin^2\theta\) to near certainty in \(\Theta(1/\sqrt{p})\) applications of \(A\) and \(A^\dagger\), achieving the optimal quadratic speedup for unstructured search.
Fixed-point phase sequences and quantum amplitude estimation avoid overshooting when \(p\) is unknown and estimate \(p\) with error \(\varepsilon\) in \(O(1/\varepsilon)\) coherent queries.
06-quantum-walks: Discrete-time coined walks and continuous-time walks \(e^{-iHt}\) replace diffusive classical spreading with ballistic wave propagation and graph-dependent interference.
Szegedy’s construction turns any reversible Markov chain into a bipartite reflection walk whose spectral gap is the square root of the classical gap.
Quantum walk search and element distinctness combine graph traversal with local marking reflections to achieve polynomial speedups over classical random walks.
07-operator-embedding: A block encoding embeds a non-unitary matrix \(A/\alpha\) into the top-left block of a larger unitary \(U\) so that \((\langle 0|_a \otimes I)U(|0\rangle_a \otimes |\psi\rangle) = (A/\alpha)|\psi\rangle\).
Linear combinations of unitaries (LCU) implement \(A = \sum_j c_j U_j\) with normalization factor \(\alpha = \sum_j |c_j|\) using a prepare–select–unprepare circuit.
Block encodings compose cleanly under sums and products, allowing complex operators to be assembled modularly while tracking the subnormalization factor \(\alpha\) and ancilla overhead.
08-polynomial-transformations: Quantum signal processing (QSP) interleaves a single-qubit signal rotation \(W(x)\) with tunable \(Z\)-phase angles to synthesize bounded degree-\(d\) polynomials \(P(x)\) of fixed parity.

Qubitization lifts QSP to any block-encoded operator \(A/\alpha\), applying a polynomial transformation \(P(A/\alpha)\) simultaneously across every singular value or eigenvalue inside invariant \(2\times 2\) subspaces.
Quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) unifies search, Hamiltonian simulation, matrix inversion, and spectral filtering under polynomial approximation theory.
09-evolution-engineering: Lie–Trotter and higher-order Suzuki product formulas approximate \(e^{-i(\sum_j H_j)t}\) by short alternating steps whose error depends on the commutators \([H_j, H_k]\) rather than the full operator norms.
LCU and QSVT simulation strategies achieve optimal query scaling in time \(t\) and precision \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) at the cost of ancilla qubits and block-encoding circuitry.

Adiabatic evolution tracks the instantaneous ground state of a slowly interpolated Hamiltonian \(H(s)\) provided the runtime scales inversely with a power of the minimum spectral gap \(\Delta_{\min}\).
10-variational-methods: Variational algorithms pair a shallow parameterized quantum circuit \(U(\boldsymbol{\theta})\) with a classical optimizer that minimizes a measured expectation value \(E(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \langle\psi(\boldsymbol{\theta})|H|\psi(\boldsymbol{\theta})\rangle\).

The parameter-shift rule evaluates exact analytic gradients on hardware by running the same circuit at shifted angles \(\theta_k \pm \pi/2\), while shot noise requires explicit measurement-budget allocation.
Expressibility and trainability stand in tension: unstructured deep ansätze suffer from barren plateaus where gradient variances decay exponentially with qubit count.
11-adaptive-measurement: Mid-circuit measurement and classical feed-forward allow subsequent quantum gates to depend on observed outcomes, trading circuit width for classical control latency.
Iterative phase estimation replaces an \(m\)-qubit Fourier register with a single recycled control qubit measured bit-by-bit from least to most significant phase digit.

Measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) prepares a fixed entangled cluster state first and drives universal unitary computation entirely through adaptive single-qubit measurements and Pauli byproduct corrections.
